question.text: A benefit of pooling offshore investor money in an offshore feeder BEFORE it reaches the Indian AIF is:

answer.text: Each individual offshore investor avoids the need to obtain an Indian PAN / file Indian returns; only the feeder fund deals with Indian tax compliance.
Offshore investors become eligible for Section 80C deductions.
The feeder fund gets SEBI AIF registration automatically.
Offshore investors get voting rights in the investee companies.

explanation.text: The Logic: A key operational advantage of feeder-level pooling is that the feeder (as one entity) interfaces with Indian tax administration. Without a feeder, each direct offshore investor would need an Indian PAN and to file Indian returns. With the feeder, only the offshore fund/feeder deals with Indian tax compliance. The Trap: Other options (Section 80C, automatic SEBI registration, voting rights in investee) are unrelated to feeder pooling. Note: The workbook supports offshore pooling reducing Indian PAN and domestic tax return filing requirements to the feeder rather than every offshore investor. Withholding-matrix detail and PMLA/look-through implementation commentary have been removed.
